ip_top_stories.title: RIAA, NMPA, and more file amicus brief backing UMG, Concord and ABKCO in original Anthropic case, arguing AI firm's unlicensed copying is 'inexcusable'
ip_top_stories.summary: Major music industry bodies including the RIAA and NMPA have filed an amicus brief supporting UMG, Concord and ABKCO in their copyright suit against Anthropic, arguing the AI company's unlicensed copying of lyrics is inexcusable. The brief adds significant industry weight to the litigation against Anthropic's training data practices.

ip_top_stories.title: Publishers Back Concord Music Group's AI Suit
ip_top_stories.summary: Publishers and media groups have filed in support of Concord Music Group's copyright lawsuit against Anthropic, according to Publishers Weekly. The move signals a broad coalition of content owners aligning against AI companies over unlicensed training data use.

ip_top_stories.title: Penguin to sue OpenAI over ChatGPT version of German children's book
ip_top_stories.summary: Penguin is preparing to sue OpenAI after ChatGPT reportedly reproduced substantial content from a German children's book, raising questions about AI reproduction of copyrighted literary works. The case follows a related story about a dragon book where ChatGPT's output closely mirrored a copyrighted text.

ip_top_stories.title: Claude Code leak puts Anthropic on the other side of the copyright battle
ip_top_stories.summary: A leak of Anthropic's Claude Code system prompt has placed the company in an awkward position, as the leaked material highlights the irony of an AI firm whose products are accused of ingesting copyrighted content now facing questions about the unauthorised exposure of its own proprietary information. Legal and ethical commentators have noted the contradiction with Anthropic's stance in ongoing copyright litigation.

ip_top_stories.title: Can AI train on digital news content? Court reserves verdict in ANI vs OpenAI case
ip_top_stories.summary: An Indian court has reserved its verdict in the case brought by news agency ANI against OpenAI, which centres on whether AI companies can lawfully train their models on digital news content. The outcome could have significant implications for AI training data practices in India and potentially beyond.

ip_further_links.title: French private members' bill aims to protect creatives' copyright from AI usage
ip_further_links.summary: A French parliamentary bill has been introduced seeking to protect creators' copyright against unauthorised AI training use.

ip_further_links.title: UK government maintains status quo on AI and copyright, playing the long game on potential reform
ip_further_links.summary: The UK government has opted to maintain its current position on AI and copyright rather than push through immediate reform, signalling a cautious approach to balancing AI innovation with creator rights.

ip_further_links.title: AI in Litigation Series: An Update on AI Copyright Cases in 2026
ip_further_links.summary: A legal roundup surveying the current landscape of AI copyright litigation in 2026, covering key cases and emerging trends.

ip_further_links.title: Anthropic's Amodei seeks copyright deal that 'works for everyone'
ip_further_links.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has indicated a desire to reach a copyright licensing arrangement that satisfies both AI developers and rights holders, including in the context of an Australian copyright dispute.

ip_further_links.title: Cloudflare Legal Chief on AI Bots and Publisher Revenue Loss
ip_further_links.summary: Cloudflare's chief legal officer discusses the impact of AI crawlers on publisher revenue and the company's approach to managing bot traffic and piracy orders.

ip_further_links.title: What AI Asks of Open Access
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how the rise of AI training on published research is challenging and reshaping open access publishing models.

ip_further_links.title: Is Copyright Law the Wrong Weapon Against AI?
ip_further_links.summary: A legal commentary piece questions whether copyright law is the most effective or appropriate tool for regulating AI training data practices.

ip_further_links.title: CNIPA Warns Against Using AI Agents Including OpenClaw in Drafting Patent Application Documents
ip_further_links.summary: China's National Intellectual Property Administration has issued a warning against the use of AI agents in drafting patent applications, citing accuracy and legal compliance concerns.

ip_further_links.title: Celebrities Are Turning to Trademark Law to Protect Their Images and Voices From AI
ip_further_links.summary: Public figures are increasingly using trademark law rather than copyright as a means of protecting their likenesses and voices from AI-generated reproductions.

ip_further_links.title: How African creators are currently being exploited in the AI boom
ip_further_links.summary: An investigation into how African creators' works are being used without consent or compensation to train AI systems, highlighting gaps in legal protection across the continent.
